prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects POST requests whose Accept header lists only application/json (without also listing text/event-stream), even though JSON response mode never opens an SSE stream. Both PRs patch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts to allow JSON-only Accept headers. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects POST requests whose Accept header lists only application/json (without also listing text/event-stream), even though JSON response mode never opens an SSE stream. Both PRs patch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts to allow JSON-only Accept headers. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 1996 replaces the check with a dedicated acceptsMediaType() helper that does proper HTTP content-negotiation parsing: it splits on media-range parameters and explicitly excludes entries with q=0 (per RFC 7231, q=0 means the client explicitly rejects that type), and is structured to also support type/subtype wildcard matching. 2046 instead swaps the && check for an includes('application/json')-style substring check, which does not account for q=0 exclusion (e.g. 'Accept: application/json;q=0' would be incorrectly accepted) and has no wildcard handling. 1996's logic is isolated in a standalone function that is easier to unit test independently, whereas 2046's fix is inlined directly into the request-handling branch.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs replace the exact same code block in buildWellKnownPath, so merging one causes a direct conflict with the other. #2214 applies the same regex-based multi-slash strip to BOTH buildWellKnownPath and buildDiscoveryUrls, which contain byte-for-byte duplicate trailing-slash-stripping logic. #2215 only rewrites buildWellKnownPath (via a new normalizeDiscoveryPath helper) and leaves buildDiscoveryUrls's identical single-slash-only strip untouched, so a pathname with multiple trailing slashes would still produce a malformed '//' discovery URL through buildDiscoveryUrls even after #2215 merges.
